entries.ex: Recent *research* suggests that regular exercise improves memory in older adults.
entries.exAr: تشير *الأبحاث* الحديثة إلى أن ممارسة الرياضة بانتظام تحسن الذاكرة لدى كبار السن.

entries.ex: Students carried out an *experiment* to test how temperature affects plant growth.
entries.exAr: أجرى الطلاب *تجربة* لاختبار تأثير درجة الحرارة في نمو النبات.

entries.ex: The researchers' *hypothesis* was that a lack of sleep reduces concentration.
entries.exAr: كانت *فرضية* الباحثين أن قلة النوم تضعف التركيز.

entries.ex: Einstein's *theory* of relativity transformed our understanding of space and time.
entries.exAr: غيّرت *نظرية* النسبية لأينشتاين فهمنا للمكان والزمان تغييرا جذريا.

entries.ex: The blood was sent to a *laboratory* for further tests.
entries.exAr: أُرسل الدم إلى *مختبر* لإجراء مزيد من الفحوص.

entries.ex: The *discovery* of a new species of frog in the rainforest surprised biologists.
entries.exAr: فاجأ *اكتشاف* نوع جديد من الضفادع في الغابة المطيرة علماء الأحياء.

entries.ex: Scientists hope for a *breakthrough* in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.
entries.exAr: يأمل العلماء في تحقيق *إنجاز كبير* في علاج مرض ألزهايمر.

entries.ex: The team used computer software to *analyse* data from thousands of patients.
entries.exAr: استخدم الفريق برنامجا حاسوبيا *لتحليل* بيانات آلاف المرضى.

entries.ex: The study was based on a *sample* of 2,000 adults from different regions.
entries.exAr: استندت الدراسة إلى *عينة* من 2000 شخص بالغ من مناطق مختلفة.

entries.ex: A national *survey* found that most people support more funding for science.
entries.exAr: وجد *استطلاع* وطني أن معظم الناس يؤيدون زيادة تمويل العلوم.

entries.ex: Careful *observation* of the birds revealed changes in their migration patterns.
entries.exAr: كشف *الرصد* الدقيق للطيور عن تغيرات في أنماط هجرتها.

entries.ex: Researchers must describe their *method* clearly so that others can repeat the study.
entries.exAr: يجب على الباحثين وصف *منهجهم* بوضوح حتى يتمكن غيرهم من تكرار الدراسة.

entries.ex: In a fair test, scientists change only one *variable* at a time.
entries.exAr: في الاختبار العادل يغيّر العلماء *متغيرا* واحدا فقط في كل مرة.

entries.ex: The northern lights are a natural *phenomenon* caused by particles from the sun.
entries.exAr: الشفق القطبي *ظاهرة* طبيعية تسببها جسيمات قادمة من الشمس.

entries.ex: *Genetic engineering* has produced crops that can survive long periods of drought.
entries.exAr: أنتجت *الهندسة الوراثية* محاصيل قادرة على تحمل فترات طويلة من الجفاف.

entries.ex: In 1996, scientists in Scotland *cloned* a sheep, Dolly, from an adult cell.
entries.exAr: في عام 1996 *استنسخ* علماء في اسكتلندا النعجة دوللي من خلية بالغة.

entries.ex: Some people believe the money spent on *space exploration* should be used to fight poverty.
entries.exAr: يرى بعض الناس أن الأموال التي تنفق على *استكشاف الفضاء* ينبغي أن تستخدم لمكافحة الفقر.

entries.ex: Weather forecasters rely on *satellites* to track storms across the ocean.
entries.exAr: يعتمد خبراء الأرصاد الجوية على *الأقمار الصناعية* لتتبع العواصف فوق المحيط.

entries.ex: Universities have committees that review the *ethics* of research involving humans.
entries.exAr: لدى الجامعات لجان تراجع *أخلاقيات* البحوث التي يشارك فيها بشر.

entries.ex: Every article in the journal goes through *peer review* before publication.
entries.exAr: يخضع كل مقال في المجلة *للتحكيم العلمي* قبل نشره.

entries.ex: The *findings* show a clear link between air pollution and asthma in children.
entries.exAr: تظهر *النتائج* وجود صلة واضحة بين تلوث الهواء والربو لدى الأطفال.

entries.ex: There is little *empirical* evidence that brain-training games improve intelligence.
entries.exAr: الأدلة *التجريبية* على أن ألعاب تدريب الدماغ تحسن الذكاء قليلة.

entries.ex: The study *investigated* the effects of screen time on children's sleep.
entries.exAr: *بحثت* الدراسة في آثار الوقت الذي يقضيه الأطفال أمام الشاشات على نومهم.

entries.ex: Scientists have not yet *proved* that the drug works for all patients.
entries.exAr: لم *يُثبت* العلماء بعد أن الدواء فعال لجميع المرضى.

entries.ex: The university *conducted* a five-year study into the causes of obesity.
entries.exAr: *أجرت* الجامعة دراسة استمرت خمس سنوات حول أسباب السمنة.

entries.ex: There is strong *scientific* agreement that human activity is warming the planet.
entries.exAr: هناك إجماع *علمي* قوي على أن النشاط البشري يؤدي إلى احترار الكوكب.

entries.ex: Official *statistics* show that the number of female engineers has risen steadily over the past decade.
entries.exAr: تظهر *الإحصاءات* الرسمية أن عدد المهندسات ارتفع بثبات خلال العقد الماضي.

entries.ex: Her research was published in a leading medical *journal*.
entries.exAr: نُشر بحثها في *مجلة* طبية رائدة.

entries.ex: Early inventors often found solutions through *trial and error*.
entries.exAr: كثيرا ما توصل المخترعون الأوائل إلى الحلول عن طريق *التجربة والخطأ*.
col: a process of trial and error

entries.ex: Doctors are expected to follow *evidence-based* guidelines when treating patients.
entries.exAr: يُتوقع من الأطباء اتباع إرشادات *قائمة على الأدلة* عند علاج المرضى.

gap.s: The study was ____ in three hospitals over a period of two years.
A larger ____ of participants would make the results more reliable.

para.a: Scientists did a test to see if the new medicine works.
para.b: Scientists carried out an *experiment* to assess whether the new drug is effective.

para.a: This idea is supported by real data, not just opinions.
para.b: This approach is *evidence-based* rather than founded on personal opinion.

para.a: People disagree a lot about whether it is right to change human genes.
para.b: The *ethics* of altering human genes remain highly controversial.

para.a: The scientists looked at the problem very carefully.

p1.q: Did you enjoy science lessons at school?
p1.a: Yes, I did, especially chemistry. I loved the practical lessons in the *laboratory*, where we could do a simple *experiment* instead of just reading the textbook. It made the subject feel real and much more exciting.

p1.q: Are you interested in science news?
p1.a: Quite interested, yes. I often read about medical *discoveries* or new technology on news websites. I find it fascinating when scientists make a *breakthrough* that could change everyday life, like a new treatment for a common disease.

p1.q: Would you like to work as a scientist?
p1.a: Honestly, I don't think so. I admire scientists, but I'm not sure I have the patience. *Research* can take years, and you might *investigate* a question for a long time without finding a clear answer.

p2.cue: Describe a scientific discovery that you think is important.
points: how it has affected people's lives
and explain why you think it is so important
p2.a: I'd like to talk about the *discovery* of penicillin, which I think is one of the most important events in medical history. It was made by a Scottish scientist called Alexander Fleming in 1928. Interestingly, it happened partly by accident. Fleming returned from a holiday and noticed that mould had grown on one of the dishes in his *laboratory*, and the bacteria around it had died. Instead of throwing the dish away, he made a careful *observation* and realised that the mould was producing something that killed germs. Later, other scientists developed his idea into a medicine that could be produced in large quantities. Before antibiotics, even a small cut could lead to a deadly infection. Since then, penicillin and similar drugs have saved millions of lives. I think it is so important not only because of its medical value, but also because it shows how curiosity and *scientific* thinking can turn a simple accident into a real *breakthrough*.

p3.q: Should governments spend more money on space exploration?
p3.a: I think a balanced approach is best. *Space exploration* has given us valuable technology, such as *satellites* that help us forecast the weather and manage disasters. However, when many people still lack clean water and healthcare, governments should make sure that spending on space does not come at the expense of urgent needs here on Earth.

p3.q: Why do some people distrust scientists?
p3.a: There are several reasons. Some people simply do not understand how science works, so when experts change their advice, it looks as if they were wrong. Also, false claims spread very quickly online. I think scientists should explain their *findings* in plain language and show the public that their advice is *evidence-based*, not just personal opinion.

speaking.tipAr: لا تجب بكلمة واحدة في الجزء الأول، بل أضف سببا أو مثالا قصيرا من تجربتك ليصل جوابك إلى جملتين أو ثلاث جمل.

writing.q: Some people think that governments should fund scientific research only if it has clear practical benefits, while others believe that all kinds of research are valuable. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay: Governments around the world spend billions on science every year, so it is natural to ask which projects deserve public money. Some people argue that only *research* with clear practical benefits should be funded, whereas others believe that all scientific enquiry has value. This essay will discuss both views before explaining why I support the second.

Those who favour practical research point out that public funds are limited and taxpayers expect results. Projects that develop vaccines, improve crop yields or reduce pollution offer direct benefits, and their *findings* can be measured. From this perspective, an expensive project that merely tests a *theory* about distant galaxies may seem difficult to justify when hospitals and schools need money. Supporters of this view also argue that funding decisions should be *evidence-based* and directed towards areas where the need is greatest.

However, history shows that it is often impossible to predict which studies will turn out to be useful. Many major *discoveries* were made by scientists who were simply curious. For example, early *experiments* on electricity had no obvious purpose at the time, yet they eventually transformed every part of modern life. Similarly, *space exploration* was once seen as a luxury, but it led to *satellite* technology that we now rely on for communication and weather forecasting. If governments funded only applied research, such unexpected *breakthroughs* might never happen.

In conclusion, although it is understandable that governments want their spending to produce practical results, I believe that basic research deserves support too. A sensible policy would fund both types, because today's curiosity often becomes tomorrow's solution.
writing.tipAr: في مقال المناقشة خصص فقرة لكل رأي واعرضه بإنصاف، ثم اذكر رأيك بوضوح في المقدمة والخاتمة.
